summary: Not on these pairs. Pooled across BTC, ETH and SOL, every setting did the same as random on 1h, 4h and daily. That covers buying the retracement of an up-leg and shorting the bounce in a down-leg. The one result that holds goes against the short: on 1h, while the pair was below its 200-day SMA, shorting a cross up through 0.705 of a down-leg did 0.24% worse than random after 20 candles.

verdicts.use: Buying the OTE retracement (up-leg crosses down 0.618 or 0.705)
verdicts.text: Same as random on 1h, 4h and daily, at 0.618 or 0.705, with or without a 3% minimum leg.

verdicts.use: Buying in discount (below 0.5 of an up-leg)
verdicts.text: Same as random on 1h, 4h and daily. On SOL 4h it looked worse than random, but only because of one stretch of signals.

verdicts.use: Shorting the OTE bounce (down-leg crosses up 0.705)
verdicts.text: Same as random pooled on 1h, 4h and daily, and in uptrends. On 1h below the 200-day SMA it did worse than random at 10 and 20 candles, because price kept rising after the bounce.
Same as random pooled on 1h, 4h and daily. The worse-than-random reading on 4h in downtrends rests on one stretch.

notes: On 1h, an up-leg retracing down through 0.705 gave 2,579 entries in 1,532 separate moves. Twenty candles later they were 0.07% behind random entries, inside the luck band of -0.19% to 0.17%. The 0.618 level fires about a fifth more often and lands in the same place. Requiring a leg of 3% or more changes nothing.

Holding a long while price sat in discount, below 0.5 of a 3%+ up-leg, enters on many candles of each move. It ended 0.04% behind random on 1h and 0.14% behind on 4h, both inside the band. On SOL 4h it was 0.59% worse than random, but that came from 64 signals on Aug 15–29, 2022. Without them, it was the same as random.

On 4h, every long setting ended behind random in uptrends and ahead of it in downtrends, all inside the luck band. The 0.705 cross was 0.34% behind in uptrends and 0.85% ahead in downtrends. On 1h the gaps were 0.13% or less either way. Neither regime turns the retracement into a timing signal.

Shorting a down-leg bounce up through 0.705 on 1h was the same as random overall and in uptrends. While the pair was below its 200-day SMA, it did 0.24% worse than random after 20 candles. That holds without its strongest stretch, on Jan 13, 2023, and at 10 candles, though not at 50 or 100. The premium short on 4h in downtrends looked worse too, but only because of signals on Jan 2–14, 2023.

Daily candles give few signals. The 0.705 cross gave 88 entries in 62 moves, 2.32% behind random inside a band of -5.34% to 5.45%, and the 3% leg filter gave the same 88 entries. Each coin alone has under 30 moves, too few to judge. So does the uptrend regime of the long cross and the downtrend regime of the short cross.

For a long DCA bot, buying at 0.618 or 0.705 timed entries no better than a random candle on these pairs, so the DCA orders and take profit do the work. You can still use the zone as a location filter beside another condition, but don't expect it to improve timing. For a short bot on 1h, consider leaving out the 0.705 bounce while the pair trades below its 200-day SMA, where those bounces tended to keep going.
